findings.finding: The plan says downstream readers need no change. But the reuse short-circuits in reuse.py read the same sidecar and attestation the agentic engine will now write, and the plan does not list them. Today `_run_plan_review` runs `reuse.idempotent_reuse`, `reuse.verdict_reuse` and `drift_refresh` only under `engine == "pipeline"`. The code comment justifying that guard ('agentic never returns a pipeline verdict') stops being true once the adapter emits agentic PASS and BLOCK. `verdict_reuse` replays the latest sidecar whenever its verdict is BLOCK and its material fingerprint and code SHA match. It never checks `coverage.engine`, so a pipeline-engine review after an agentic BLOCK would return the agentic blockers without running the pipeline. Likewise `idempotent_reuse` accepts any valid attestation, so an agentic-signed PASS would short-circuit a later pipeline review. Meanwhile agentic runs never reuse anything, so every agentic re-review is billed again even when its own attestation is current.
findings.location: Approach > 'The real post-dispatch path' / Scope (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py and plan_review/__init__.py:542-554 not addressed)
scenarios: An operator runs `review-plan --engine agentic`, gets an agentic BLOCK, then reruns with `--engine pipeline` on the unchanged plan. verdict_reuse replays the agentic blockers as the pipeline result, and no pipeline review runs.
An agentic PASS signs. A later pipeline review is skipped by idempotent_reuse, so the side-by-side comparison of the engines never actually runs the pipeline.
Repeated agentic reviews of an unchanged, already-certified plan each make a new billable frontier agent call, because reuse is disabled under agentic.

findings.finding: Agentic PASS attestations and BLOCK sidecars will be read by pipeline-only reuse shortcuts that do not check which engine produced them. Until now the agentic engine only emitted unsigned INDETERMINATE verdicts (floor verdicts aside), so reuse.verdict_reuse, reuse.idempotent_reuse and orchestrator.drift_refresh never saw an agentic PASS or BLOCK. After this change, a later `engine=pipeline` run on an unchanged plan will replay a stored agentic BLOCK (blocking findings with tier AGENTIC, plus the stored coverage, including coverage.engine='agentic') as its own result without running the pipeline. It will also reuse or drift-refresh an agentic-signed PASS. The plan says downstream readers 'need no change' and defers only the attestation `engine` field, so it takes no position on cross-engine reuse.

findings.finding: The plan says that passing RunnerAgentStep.last_error makes _degraded_plan_review_verdict record the failure class for every failure listed (provider error, refusal, timeout, limit exhaustion, truncation, schema-invalid output). The code does not support that. A failure class only reaches coverage when the raised exception carries an `.outcome`, and only the generic provider-failure arm of run_failure.interpret_failure attaches one. A step-budget overrun is raised as LLMBudgetExhaustedError with only `.diagnostic` set. RunawayToolLoopError, and any existing LLMError such as UnretryableOutputError (truncation, bad stop reason) or StructuredOutputError (schema-invalid output), are re-raised with no `.outcome`. For those failures outcome_of() returns None, resolution_fields() returns {}, and no resolution_class is written. degrade_cause_flags() also stamps them llm_unavailable=True, so they read like a provider outage.
findings.location: Approach → Failed and degraded runs (RunnerAgentStep last_error bullet); Testing → Failure
scenarios: The agent uses up its 156-iteration budget: the verdict is INDETERMINATE with no resolution_class and llm_unavailable=True, so it looks like a provider outage and the retryable exit-11 disposition is missing.
The agent's output is truncated (finish_reason=length → UnretryableOutputError): no failure class is recorded.
The plan's only failure test uses an LLMUnavailableError that already carries an outcome, so it passes without exercising either of these cases.
findings.suggested_fix: In the agentic degrade branch, if failure.outcome_of(last_error) is None and last_error is an exception, attach `last_error.outcome = classify_llm_failure(last_error, ClassifyContext(model=<frontier model>))` before calling _degraded_plan_review_verdict. Extend the Testing section with budget-exhaustion and truncation cases that assert a non-empty resolution_class.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Filter agent `criteria` against the same set `criteria_context(ctx.repo_root)` offers (by_id(ctx.repo_root) minus DET and nameless entries), and add a test that a P-id and `prerequisite-consistency` are dropped.
evidence: Plan: "`criteria` filtered to ids in `registry.by_id()` (may be empty)"
agentic.py:77-88 criteria_context: `registry.by_id(repo_root)` filtered by `crit.get('name') and crit.get('exec') != _DET_EXEC`
registry.py:354-366 by_id(repo_root=None) always adds the synthetic `prerequisite-consistency`; load_criteria resolves the repo from repo_root
findings.finding: The adapter accepts a different set of criteria ids than the prompt offers the agent. The prompt's REVIEW CRITERIA list is `criteria_context(ctx.repo_root)`: registry.by_id(repo_root) minus DET criteria (P1-P11) and nameless entries such as `prerequisite-consistency`. The adapter filters against plain `registry.by_id()`. As written, this keeps DET floor ids and `prerequisite-consistency`, which the agent was never offered. Because the call omits repo_root, it can also resolve a different repo's overlay than the one the prompt was built from, and so drop activated `project.*` criteria the agent was shown.
findings.location: Approach › Adapter ("`criteria` filtered to ids in `registry.by_id()`")
scenarios: The agent tags a finding P8 (seen in the plan text). The adapter keeps it, so the agentic finding shows up as a DET-floor criterion
A project criterion offered in the prompt is dropped because by_id() ran without ctx.repo_root
findings.suggested_fix: Expose a helper in agentic.py, e.g. `offered_criteria_ids(repo_root)`, that returns the same ids criteria_context lists. Use it both to render the prompt and to filter in adapt_findings, called with ctx.repo_root.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that RunnerAgentStep resets `last_error` at the start of each `run()` call, records the exception before re-raising it, and that the agentic degrade uses `last_error` only when it is set (otherwise `res.error`); add a test where the adapter op raises.
evidence: Plan: "`RunnerAgentStep` ... keeps the last exception its runner raised (`last_error`). Under `engine == "agentic"`, `produce_plan_review_verdict`'s final degrade passes that exception instead of the error string"
runs.py:301-306 calls `runner.run(req)` with only a try/finally, so no exception is recorded today; interpreter.py:517-518 turns any step exception into `StepResult(status='failed', error=str(exc))`
gate_dispatch.py:285-291: the final degrade passes `error=(res.error or ...)`; plan_review_recovery.py:392 writes `"llm_error": str(error)`
The Testing section covers only a runner that raises (LLMUnavailableError, RuntimeError), not a non-runner step failure
findings.finding: The `last_error` fallback is underspecified in two ways. (1) Placement: the plan does not say whether RunnerAgentStep.run resets `last_error` at the start of each call, or that it must record the exception and then re-raise it so the interpreter still fails the step. (2) Fallback: the plan has no rule for when `last_error` is None, or describes a different failure than the one that ended the run. Under engine=='agentic', the run can also fail with no runner exception at all: the agentic_inputs op raises, the agentic_verdict adapter op raises, or the new det_*/hierarchy inputs break the input contract (interpreter `input contract violation`). In each case the final degrade would get None (or a stale exception) in place of `res.error`. coverage.llm_error would then read 'None' and the real failure cause would be lost.
findings.location: Approach › Failed and degraded runs (RunnerAgentStep `last_error`; produce_plan_review_verdict final degrade)
scenarios: The adapter op raises (for example, a KeyError on a malformed finding) after a successful agent call: last_error is None, and the verdict records llm_error='None'
An input-contract violation on agentic_verdict's new det_* inputs fails the step with no runner exception
findings.suggested_fix: In RunnerAgentStep.run: set `self.last_error = None` on entry, wrap `runner.run(req)` in `except Exception as exc: self.last_error = exc; raise`. In the agentic degrade: `error = agent_step.last_error or res.error or 'plan-review workflow LLM tier failed'`. Add a test where `plan_review_agentic_verdict` raises and assert that llm_error carries that op's error string.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Filter agent finding criteria against the same set criteria_context rendered (registry.by_id(ctx.repo_root), named, non-DET), not bare registry.by_id(), and add a test for a project criterion id and a DET id.
evidence: agentic.criteria_context uses `registry.by_id(repo_root)` and keeps only entries with `crit.get("name") and crit.get("exec") != _DET_EXEC`.
registry.by_id(repo_root=None) builds from load_criteria(repo_root) and always adds a synthetic 'prerequisite-consistency' entry with default_posture 'blocking'.
findings.finding: The criteria filter is specified as 'criteria filtered to ids in `registry.by_id()`'. That set is not the one the agent was shown. criteria_context(repo_root) gives the agent the effective registry for the repo (including activated project criteria), minus DET-exec criteria and nameless synthetic entries. `registry.by_id()` with no repo_root loads the default criteria set, so ids of project criteria the agent was shown can be dropped. It also always includes the DET floor ids (P1-P11) and the synthetic 'prerequisite-consistency' entry, so an agent finding tagged with those is kept even though they were deliberately left out of the prompt. 'prerequisite-consistency' has default_posture 'blocking', so it also affects _any_blocking_criterion.
findings.location: Approach → Adapter, field-mapping bullet ('criteria filtered to ids in registry.by_id()'); src/rebar/llm/plan_review/agentic.py:77-88; src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:354-366
scenarios: A repo with an activated project criterion: the agent tags a finding with that id, and the adapter strips it, losing the criterion link in coaching, guide_url and the sidecar.
The agent tags a finding 'P8' or 'prerequisite-consistency': the adapter keeps a criterion the agent was never asked to judge.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the id set out of criteria_context into a helper such as `agentic.llm_criterion_ids(repo_root) -> set[str]` (named, exec != 'DET', from registry.by_id(repo_root)). Use it in both criteria_context and adapt_findings so the prompt and the filter cannot drift apart.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace `disposition` with the fields resolution_fields() actually writes (`resolution_class`, `retryable`, `diagnostic`) and pin those in the failure test.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/failure.py:396-408: resolution_fields returns {resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic}; its docstring calls it "the single writer of the disposition shape onto `coverage`".
Searching src/rebar/llm for the string "disposition" finds only the prerequisite-coverage records (decide_ops.py, prerequisites.py, workflow_ops.py), never verdict coverage.
findings.finding: The plan says the degraded verdict records the failure class as `resolution_class` and `disposition`. failure.resolution_fields(), the only function that writes the disposition onto coverage, writes `resolution_class`, `retryable` and `diagnostic`. No `disposition` key is written onto plan-review verdict coverage anywhere. A test or reader written against `coverage.disposition` would fail or read nothing.
findings.location: Approach → Failed and degraded runs ("records the failure class (`resolution_class`, `disposition`)")
scenarios: An implementer pins `coverage['disposition']` in test_plan_review_agentic_verdict.py and the test fails, or they add a new field the existing CLIs do not read.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the parenthetical to "(`resolution_class`, `retryable`, `diagnostic`)" and have the failure test assert resolution_class and retryable.

findings.finding: The plan says the degrade records the failure class as "(`resolution_class`, `disposition`)", but no `disposition` coverage field exists. The single writer, failure.resolution_fields, emits `resolution_class`, `retryable` and `diagnostic`, and those are the keys the verdict schema's coverage defines. An executor following the plan literally might add a non-existent `disposition` key, or test for one.
findings.location: Approach › Failed and degraded runs (first bullet)
scenarios: A test asserts `coverage['disposition']` and fails, or someone adds a new ad-hoc key to coverage
